headline: Cloudflare has released two downloadable AI models, Clef and Clef-Flash, that pick from fixed answers to help AI agents decide.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered 2: the release is older news, first carried in our 2 Oct 2026 edition, and this article adds detail but no new event.
importance_line: Teams that route support requests or other tasks through AI agents could use these models for quick decisions, but the benchmark results come from Cloudflare and commenters question them.
summary: InfoQ reports, citing Cloudflare's blog, that Clef is a 27-billion-parameter model that returns a probability for each allowed answer, and that the smaller Clef-Flash runs at a median 38.8 milliseconds against 209.3 for Clef. This repeats our 2 Oct 2026 report of the same release, and the detail here is mainly the speed figures.
notes: Repeat: our 2 Oct 2026 edition carried this release (Cloudflare's blog, CONFIRMED). InfoQ says 'recent Birthday Week' with no date. Score lowered 2 for stale and repeat; the 14-day check (check_dup14.py) should drop it. Not the same as AWS Strands Decider 2B.
